parts: Did Paris really eat the zoo? Not all of Paris.
During the siege, Goncourt noted that a National Guard soldier earned thirty sous a day. That is a franc and a half.
On December thirty-first, Goncourt saw the trunk of young Pollux, an elephant, for sale. The butcher said forty francs a pound.
Our arithmetic: forty francs is about twenty-seven days of that pay, for one pound.
Labouchère wrote that in fashionable restaurants the supply was unlimited, and so was the price.
The idea that all Paris dined on the zoo: myth. The zoo was for those who could pay: documented.
